# 1 Enoch Chapter 12 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 12 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 12:1 — 'hidden' vs. 'vanished' for Enoch's mysterious departure

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Enoch was-hidden" | The Ge'ez verb is passive; someone/something concealed him |
| LOGOS | "Enoch had been hidden" | Same passive; pluperfect preserves the sequence |
| PNEUMA | "Enoch had vanished" | Dynamic — 'vanished' captures the mystery but loses the passive (implies active departure) |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'Enoch had been hidden' (LOGOS). The passive is theologically significant — this is divine concealment, not Enoch's own disappearance (cf. Gen 5:24: 'God took him'). PNEUMA's 'vanished' mistakenly implies self-initiated withdrawal.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 12:3 — 'Lord of majesty' title

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Lord of-majesty" | Preserves the Ge'ez construct literally |
| LOGOS | "Lord of majesty" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "Lord of majesty" | All three agree |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Unanimous agreement on 'Lord of majesty.' This is a key divine title in 1 Enoch; all three translators preserved it identically.

**Status:** Unanimous.

---

## 12:4 — 'scribe of righteousness' vs. 'righteous scribe'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Enoch the-scribe of-righteousness" | Ge'ez construct chain: 'scribe' qualified by 'of righteousness' |
| LOGOS | "scribe of righteousness" | Same construct; the title is a technical designation |
| PNEUMA | "righteous scribe" | Inverts the construct to English adjective-noun order |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'scribe of righteousness' (EMET/LOGOS). The construct form is a technical title; inverting it to 'righteous scribe' loses the titular force. 'Scribe of righteousness' echoes the Hebrew/Aramaic genre of the professional scribe who specializes in legal/covenantal documents.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 12:5-6 — Register of the judgment speech

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Formal legal register with archaic constructions | Preserves the solemn juridical tone |
| LOGOS | Formal English, legal register maintained | Clear and formal without EMET's archaism |
| PNEUMA | More colloquial, dialogue-like | Accessible but loses the solemnity of the decree |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS formal register for the judgment speech. The decree in vv. 5–6 is a juridical pronouncement, and its formal register signals its authoritative status. PNEUMA's colloquial tone undermines this.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## Overall assessment

Chapter 12 opens the Enoch-commission narrative and contains several significant translational decisions, particularly around the passive 'hidden' (v. 1), the title 'scribe of righteousness' (vv. 3–4), and the register of the judgment speech (vv. 5–6). Total significant divergences: 4.
